SevenUI is a registry of 65 primitives built on Base UI. Primitives are installed as source code into your project through the shadcn CLI — no runtime package to depend on. Composed, copy-and-go usage of these primitives lives in Components; full pro sections and pages live in Blocks. Why SevenUI Base UI first — no Radix, anywhere. Every interactive part is built on Base UI; the only exceptions are four sanctioned, Radix-free specialized libraries (calendar, carousel, chart, resizable). Drop-in shadcn compatibility — works with the shadcn CLI and your existing components.json setup. Source distribution via the registry — primitives install as source files you own, not a package you depend on. Coverage SevenUI ships 65 primitives. The first 53 arrived across five waves: Foundation wave (15): button, badge, kbd, card, alert, separator, skeleton, spinner, aspect-ratio, textarea, table, breadcrumb, pagination, avatar, progress. Form wave (14): input, label, field, form, checkbox, radio-group, switch, toggle, toggle-group, slider, number-field, input-otp, select, combobox. Overlay wave (11): dialog, alert-dialog, sheet, drawer, popover, hover-card, tooltip, dropdown-menu, context-menu, menubar, toast. Navigation & composite wave (9): tabs, accordion, collapsible, navigation-menu, scroll-area, toolbar, meter, command, sidebar. Third-party wrapper wave (4): calendar, carousel, chart, resizable. Navigation and composition are complete — tabs, menus, a shared-popup navigation menu, a command palette, and a full sidebar system — with zero Radix dependencies. No Radix, no cmdk, no vaul, no sonner: every primitive that can be built on Base UI alone uses Base UI and nothing else. The third-party wrapper wave adds exactly four specialized, Radix-free libraries — react-day-picker, embla-carousel, recharts, and react-resizable-panels — for the primitives that genuinely cannot be built on Base UI alone, the same sanctioned choices shadcn makes. These four are the only non-Base-UI dependencies in the registry. Form primitives use Base UI-native form handling. Libraries like react-hook-form plug into the Field primitive’s external-state props — see Field. Ready to add your first primitive? Head over to Installation. Was this page helpful?
